name: Facet
text: Ship the pre-submission contrast blocker. It stops bad contrast from ever reaching the screen, saving us from last-minute fixes and inconsistent themes. The trade-off is we lose the flexibility to tweak contrast after submission, but that’s a feature—bad contrast never makes it in.

name: Pane
text: The real risk is training users to ignore the contrast problem—once they see it blocked pre-submission, they’ll assume it’s handled and stop checking. A better alternative is a live contrast checker in the editor that flags issues in real time without blocking submission, forcing users to engage with the problem instead of avoiding it. Settle it with a quick user test: measure how often users override the blocker versus how often they fix contrast issues when alerted live.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submission blocker trains users to treat contrast as someone else’s problem—once they see it stopped cold, they’ll stop noticing it entirely. A live checker in the editor flags issues without blocking submission, forcing users to engage with contrast as they work, not just when we force them to. Settle it with a small user test: compare submission success rates and post-submission contrast complaints between the two approaches.
